title: The Cathedral Bleeds
text: The great cathedral's walls have begun to bleed from the joints between the stones, and the nave is ankle-deep. The bishop says the building is dying and will take the city's faith with it. The masons blame the mortar; they want stone and gold to rebuild the north wall before it falls on the congregation.

temptation.label: Bottle the blood and sell it as a relic.
temptation.text: The pilgrims will pay anything for a vial. If the bishop finds out who sells it, he will preach against them.

triumph.text: The north wall is rebuilt and the bleeding stops. On the first Sunday the whole city fills the nave to sing; for an hour, the Rift is silent.

holds.text: The patched wall stands. The blood dries brown in the joints, and nobody washes it off.

falters.text: The north wall comes down during the evening office. The bishop is pulled alive from the rubble. He has not stopped praying since.

calamity.text: The cathedral falls. In the morning its bells are found upright in the square, ringing on their own. For a long time after, the city's prayers go unanswered.
